# AI evaluation (generated by `python -m scripts.evaluate_ai`)

All numbers below are measured, not edited. Synthetic / placeholder data only.

## Description classifier (check 26, 27)

Data: `data/descriptions_labeled.csv` — 75 rows (**placeholder written by the AI assistant, not clinician-reviewed**), split 70/30 stratified, seed 0 → train 52, test 23.
Predictions below confidence 0.45 are reported as `unclear` (what the clinician would see).

```
                          precision    recall  f1-score   support

                 absence       0.00      0.00      0.00         5
focal_impaired_awareness       1.00      0.20      0.33         5
generalized_tonic_clonic       0.00      0.00      0.00         5
               myoclonic       0.00      0.00      0.00         5
                 unclear       0.14      1.00      0.25         3

                accuracy                           0.17        23
               macro avg       0.23      0.24      0.12        23
            weighted avg       0.24      0.17      0.11        23

```

Confusion matrix (rows = true, columns = predicted):

| true \ pred | absence | focal_impaired_awareness | generalized_tonic_clonic | myoclonic | unclear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| absence | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| focal_impaired_awareness | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| generalized_tonic_clonic | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 4 |
| myoclonic | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| unclear | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 |

Without the `unclear` threshold (raw top choice), test accuracy = 0.565. The gap shows how often the model is not confident enough on this tiny training set.

Overall test accuracy: 0.174 (n=23)

## Seizure-risk estimate (check 28, 29)

Held-out synthetic patients: 45 (train: 105). Rows = one weekly snapshot per patient over the last 10 weeks: test n=405 (114 positive).
Thresholds chosen on TRAIN only (Youden J): model 0.255, baseline 0.287.

| | ROC AUC | Brier (lower = better) | sensitivity | false-alarm rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| model risk-0.1.0 | 0.533 | 0.209 | 0.395 | 0.375 |
| baseline: seizures in last 4 weeks | 0.511 | 0.210 | 0.596 | 0.595 |

AUC difference model − baseline: +0.022, 95 % patient-bootstrap interval [-0.046, +0.078]; Brier difference -0.001.

**Does the model beat the baseline?** No — not demonstrably: the interval includes zero, so the difference may be noise. Both are close to chance (AUC 0.5) on this task. This is synthetic data generated with known rules; a model trained on it mostly recovers those rules. It proves the pipeline works, not that it is clinically valid.

Synthetic demographics do not change seizure behaviour in the generator, so subgroup gaps here reflect sample size, not real-world bias. Real bias can only be measured on real local data.
